Hi Caroline / Sam,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — excited by the potential alignment. Attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a short doc that enumerates the acceptance-test vectors we propose for the evaluation phase. Quick overview of what we included: 

- Success buckets: functional correctness (extraction & intent), latency/SLO, reliability (error rate, token failures), and safety/PII filtering checks.
- Exit gates: pass on smoke vectors + no critical safety failures + readiness for production configuration.
- Quantitative thresholds (proposed): 95th percentile end-to-end latency < 400ms for 4k context half-load; 98% KV-cache hit rate for repeated prefixes; intent/rerank top-1 accuracy >= 91% on the provided test set; extraction F1 >= 0.88 on the labeled sample.
- Evidence artifacts: automatic logs (token-level latency histograms), sample outputs (50 labelled cases), post-run concordance report, and a short video walkthrough for any failing cases.

I've also proposed two tiers of acceptance: a "smoke signoff" required to progress to a pilot and a stricter "production-ready" signoff for cutover. The MAP spreadsheet maps owners, deadlines, and the minimal evidence bundle for each gate.

Attachments: MedFocus_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP workbook), acceptance-test-vectors.md (test descriptions). Also linking a short SLA proposal PDF for the Dedicated plan.

Ask: can you confirm 1) the test window you'd like us to run (we've penciled in a 7-day run starting 2026-07-20), and 2) whether your team needs additional instrumentation (trace hooks, sample IDs) added to the outputs?

I'll loop in infra/ops for any extra hooks once you confirm.

Thanks,
Irene Choi

Thanks, Irene — this looks thorough and appreciate the concrete thresholds. A couple of clarifying questions from our side before we confirm dates: 

1) Latency: our primary concern is P95 tail and occasional spikes when batch windows close. The 400ms P95 you call out is acceptable only if the P99 stays below ~1s. Can you confirm the P99 target you can commit to for the smoke window?

2) Data retention & logs: for compliance we need a record of inference inputs + model outputs for 30 days (redacted for PHI). Can Redwood supply a hashed-input log and a per-request trace id that ties into our audit trail?

3) Evaluation sampling: we can provide a 200-case labeled set for extraction tests. Will Redwood run both deterministic and sampled temperature runs (0.0 and 0.4) so we can compare regression sensitivity?

If those are doable we can confirm the 7-day window. Also copying procurement (sam) — we'll need the SLA proposal and a PO path for a short pilot.

— Caroline
Caroline Baxter
Director, Product Strategy | MedFocus Health

Caroline / Sam — thanks for the quick clarifications. Confirming the agreed commitments and timeline below so procurement can build the PO and we can schedule the run.

Agreed acceptance/exit criteria (smoke -> pilot progression):
- Smoke signoff (required to proceed to pilot):
  * Run window: 7 calendar days (recommended start: 2026-07-20)
  * Performance: P95 end-to-end latency < 400ms; P99 end-to-end latency < 1.0s (measured under the agreed synthetic traffic profile).
  * Reliability: request error rate < 0.5% (5xx + infra failures) over the run window.
  * Functional: extraction F1 >= 0.88 on the 200-case labeled set at temperature 0.0; intent rerank top-1 >= 91% at temperature 0.0.
  * Safety: zero critical safety violations on the safety vector set (defined in acceptance-test-vectors.md).
  * Evidence: hashed-input log + per-request trace ids (retained 30 days), token-level latency histogram, 50 sample cases with human labels and commentary.

- Production-ready signoff (post-pilot — checklist items to be completed during pilot):
  * Operational: KV cache hit rate improvement > baseline, autoscale runbook validated, canary rollback verified.
  * Contractual: SLA attachment signed and PO received.

Operational commitments from Redwood:
- We will provide a hashed-input + output log (SHA-256) export, per-request trace IDs, and a Drive folder with all evidence artifacts exported at the end of the 7-day run.
- We will run two passes for the 200-case labeled set: temperature 0.0 (deterministic with seed) and 0.4 (sampled). Both runs will be included in the evidence pack.
- Karthik's infra note: the P99 < 1s target is achievable with the recommended model/config (redwood/fast-8K-fp16-equivalent) using burst smoothing and a max-batch-size of 8. Estimated incremental cost for that config is ~12% over the baseline trial config (we'll surface exact numbers in the cost attachment).

Next steps and owners:
- Procurement / PO: MedFocus to share PO path; Redwood (Lauren) to provide final SLA + invoice cadence (target by 2026-07-16).
- Run scheduling: tentatively start 2026-07-20 (Irene / Avery to confirm infra warm-up on 2026-07-19).
- Evidence artifacts: acceptance-test-vectors.md will be used for scoring; Redwood to deliver the evidence folder within 48 hours of run completion.

Attachments: SLA-proposal.pdf (redwood SLA baseline).

If this summary matches your expectations please reply "Agreed" and procurement can proceed. Happy to hop on a 20-minute call if you want to walk through the test vectors before the run.

Best,
